rows.statement: A generated local mount unit gains After=local-fs-pre.target and Before=local-fs.target, and the Before= leg is dropped when nofail or an explicit wanted-by/required-by option is present.
rows.quote: automatically gain an After= dependency on local-fs-pre.target, and a Before= dependency on local-fs.target unless one or more mount options among nofail

rows.statement: nofail makes the target only want the mount instead of requiring it and removes the ordering, so boot proceeds whether or not the mount point can be mounted.
rows.quote: With nofail, this mount will be only wanted, not required, by local-fs.target or remote-fs.target.

measured.quote: local-fs.target.wants fast.mount systemd-remount-fs.service tmp.mount ### local-fs.target.requires -.mount boot.mount home.mount

rows.statement: noauto keeps the generated mount unit out of the target dependency set, so the file system is not mounted during boot unless another unit pulls it in.
rows.quote: With noauto, the mount unit will not be added as a dependency for local-fs.target or remote-fs.target.

rows.statement: When x-systemd.automount is present the generated automount unit is added to the target instead, and the auto and noauto options have no effect at all.
rows.quote: Note that if x-systemd.automount (see above) is used, neither auto nor noauto have any effect.

rows.statement: x-systemd.before= and x-systemd.after= add an ordering dependency on another unit to the created mount unit, which is the way a nofail entry re-acquires an ordering it otherwise loses.
rows.quote: In the created mount unit, configures a Before= or After= dependency on another systemd unit, such as a mount unit.

rows.statement: x-systemd.device-timeout= bounds how long the generated device unit is waited for, and the option is honoured only in fstab and ignored inside a unit file's Options= setting.
rows.quote: Configure how long systemd should wait for a device to show up before giving up on an entry from /etc/fstab.

rows.statement: x-systemd.requires= and x-systemd.wants= add Requires= or Wants= plus After= against another unit, and they always attach to the created mount unit even under automount.
rows.quote: Configures a Requires= and an After= dependency between the created mount unit and another systemd unit, such as a device or mount unit.

rows.statement: x-systemd.wanted-by= and x-systemd.required-by= replace the generated target dependencies apart from umount.target, so ordering usually has to be restored by hand.
rows.quote: In the created mount unit, configures a WantedBy= or RequiredBy= dependency on another unit.
